Artifact-first is not merely the common cold-boot order, it is STRUCTURAL: the kernel runs init-all (Phase 1) then start-all (Phase 2), the artifact reaches the registry in Phase 1 (AppPlugin.init -> manifest.register -> ObjectQL.registerApp, composite key pkgid:name) and sys_metadata rehydration runs in Phase 2 (ObjectQLPlugin.start -> restoreMetadataFromDb -> loadMetaFromDb -> hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry, bare key, no packageId). So at a cold boot the overlay is ALWAYS the second arrival and the existing `packageId &&` guard is unreachable; it fires only for a late registration (marketplace install, post-start manifest.register, HMR). Confirmed both in source and on a real @objectstack/example-crm boot (log: `Phase 1: Init plugins` 01:33:17.716, `Registering App Service {appId: com.example.crm}` 01:33:18.192, `Phase 2: Start plugins` 01:33:18.209). Fix: a second guard for the cold-boot direction, with its OWN message rather than one widened to fit both — the two orders reach the same end state (the runtime row wins either way) but differ in the event an operator acts on (a package dead on arrival behind a pre-existing row, vs a stored row taking over a definition just loaded from code), and a merged message would have to drop which one arrived second. Clause 2 is NO and was checked rather than assumed: collection.set(storageKey, item) and getItem are untouched, and the pin asserts precedence in both orders. Refusing the collision instead of warning was considered and rejected — it would break the sanctioned ADR-0005 customization path and would be an accept/reject door, i.e. a different card. #12015 trap checked by measurement, not argument: 0 lines on a stock boot (a stock sys_metadata holds no overlay of a packaged name — loadMetaFromDb returned loaded: 0 on the real CRM boot), and thereafter once per shadowed name per process, bounded by `!collection.has(bareKey)` so the line marks the transition into the bare slot rather than the state (without it the read-side hydration and the write-through would re-emit on every GET of a customized item). Known amplification, stated rather than left to be found: a customized view container expands into its ViewItems, so 1 customization produced 4 lines in the CRM measurement. Nothing touches #12399, #12401 or #12340's surfaces. One process note for the PM: REST answers 403 from this seat (#12123, measured — `GitHub access is not enabled for this session`), so the PR and the finding card were created through MCP; the dedup read before filing #12431 could not use the prescribed REST channel and fell back to a local tree grep, declared in that card's body.",

SUITES: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run` -> `Test Files 236 passed (236)` / `Tests 4185 passed (4185)`; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck` green. Targeted downstream sweep, declared as targeted rather than the full consumer closure: @objectstack/metadata-protocol (the caller of the bare-key hydration path) `Test Files 141 passed | 2 skipped (143)` / `Tests 1950 passed | 10 skipped (1960)`, and @objectstack/service-automation (whose flow-name-shadowing fixture is written against this warning) `Test Files 90 passed (90)` / `Tests 1080 passed (1080)`. GATES derived not recalled: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, self-reporting `gate list derived from the tree of 'objectstack-ai/objectstack' at commit 1fc7e3b056` — 20 matched families + 6 convention-triggered, every one exit 0 into its own log file. Verdict lines quoted: `check-type-check-coverage: OK — 65/78 workspace packages type-checked (plus the root), 13 in the DEBT ledger (382 frozen raw errors), 1 exempt.`; `check-type-check-coverage --re-measure: OK — 32 ledger entr(ies) re-measured in 249.1s, 1843 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number.` with `surplus: none — every entry sits exactly at its measurement, so any new error is red.` (run after `turbo run build --filter=./packages/* --filter=./packages/*/*` -> `Tasks: 70 successful, 70 total`, so the new test file really was measured); `check-nul-bytes: OK`. Repo-wide lint NOT narrowed: `pnpm lint` (eslint . --no-inline-config) over the whole tree, 63s, exit 0 — no narrowing claimed and none owed. ABLATION, two legs, direction predicted IN WRITING before either run, implementation committed first. REBUILD: none owed and here is why — the pin imports './registry', a relative source specifier inside its own package, so vitest resolves TypeScript source and not exports -> dist; the reds are therefore evidence about the mutation, not about a stale artifact. MUTATION PROVEN ON DISK by single-line `grep -cF` anchor counts BEFORE any result was read, and each restore leg proved absence the same way plus an empty `git diff`; the script carried `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` and it fired on both legs (`TRAP-RESTORED`). LEG A (delete the whole cold-boot guard = origin/main's registerItem): anchors `      let shadowed: any;` 1 -> 0 and `just been registered from sys_metadata.` 1 -> 0; predicted 4 of 11 red naming each case; observed `Tests 4 failed | 7 passed (11)`, exactly the four named, the first failing `AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0` — which IS the card's measurement reproduced (0 collision lines in the artifact-first order) while the LATE-REGISTRATION ORDER case stayed green in the same run. LEG B (keep the guard, drop only `&& !collection.has(bareKey)`): anchor `if (!packageId && !collection.has(bareKey)) {` 1 -> 0 and injected `if (!packageId) {` 0 -> 1; predicted exactly 1 red; observed `Tests 1 failed | 10 passed (11)`, that case, `AssertionError: expected [ …(2) ] to deeply equal []`. Leg B is the one that matters for grading: five of the six silence cases pass with OR without the guard, so they are narrowing pins against the opposite mutation rather than restatements of the defect, and without leg B nothing in the file would fail if the warning started printing on every read-side hydration. Post-restore: `git diff --stat` empty, anchors back to 1, and the pin re-ran 11/11 green.",
```json
  "open_questions": [],
  "out_of_scope_findings": [
    "filed as #12431: the overlay row's own package_id is read at hydration but dropped before registerItem (mergeArtifactProtection stamps the artifact's _packageId/_provenance onto the overlay body first), so the registry cannot distinguish a deliberate customization from an accidental name collision — which is why this card's new message has to state both readings instead of naming the one that happened. Labelled `finding`, no pm:queue, unassigned."
  ]
}
```

**ACCEPT** — PR #12430. Every fence I set was discharged by measurement, and the card's premise came back **stronger** than it was filed.

### The asymmetry is STRUCTURAL, not statistical

I asked it to *"establish which order is actually the common cold boot rather than taking the card's word for it — the whole severity argument rests on that."* The answer is better than "common":

> The kernel runs **init-all (Phase 1)** then **start-all (Phase 2)**. The artifact reaches the registry in Phase 1 (`AppPlugin.init` → `manifest.register` → `ObjectQL.registerApp`, composite key `pkgid:name`); `sys_metadata` rehydration runs in Phase 2 (`ObjectQLPlugin.start` → `restoreMetadataFromDb` → … → `hydrateOverlayIntoRegistry`, **bare key, no packageId**).

⇒ **At a cold boot the overlay is ALWAYS the second arrival, and the existing `packageId &&` guard is unreachable.** It fires only for a *late* registration — marketplace install, post-start `manifest.register`, HMR.

So the card's "silent in the common order" understates it: the warning is not merely unlikely to fire at cold boot, it **cannot**. Confirmed in source *and* on a real `@objectstack/example-crm` boot with timestamps (`Phase 1: Init plugins` 01:33:17.716 → `Registering App Service` …:18.192 → `Phase 2: Start plugins` …:18.209).

### Two messages, not one widened to fit both — and the reason is right

I flagged that *"a single message that fits both may be worse than two accurate ones."* It took the two-message route with the sharper justification:

> the two orders reach the same end state (the runtime row wins either way) but differ in **the event an operator acts on** — a package dead on arrival behind a pre-existing row, vs a stored row taking over a definition just loaded from code — and a merged message would have to drop **which one arrived second**.

That is the distinction that matters to the person reading the log at 3am.

### ⭐ The #12015 trap was checked by measurement, not by argument

This was the fence I cared most about, because #12015's first shape fired 116 times on a stock boot and said something untrue.

> **0 lines on a stock boot** — a stock `sys_metadata` holds no overlay of a packaged name; `loadMetaFromDb` returned `loaded: 0` on the real CRM boot. Thereafter **once per shadowed name per process**, bounded by `!collection.has(bareKey)` so the line marks **the transition into the bare slot rather than the state** — without it, the read-side hydration and the write-through would re-emit on every GET of a customized item.

And the amplification is **stated rather than left to be found**: a customized view container expands into its ViewItems, so 1 customization produced 4 lines in the CRM measurement. That is exactly the number a reviewer would otherwise discover in production.

### ⭐ Leg B is the leg that earns the grade

> five of the six silence cases pass **with OR without** the guard, so they are narrowing pins against the opposite mutation rather than restatements of the defect, and **without leg B nothing in the file would fail if the warning started printing on every read-side hydration**.

Naming which of your own pins are non-discriminating — and building the one leg that covers the gap — is the difference between a suite and a pin set. Leg A meanwhile **reproduced the card's measurement exactly** (`expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0` in the artifact-first order) while the late-registration case stayed green **in the same run**, which is the asymmetry demonstrated rather than described.

### ⭐ Serial constraints cleared by listing files, not trusting my globs

> PR #12396 **declares** `packages/objectql/**` but actually touches `hook-wrappers.ts`, `hook-input-mutation-traps.test.ts`, `runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts`, `hook-input-delete-writeback.test.ts` and a changeset — **disjoint from `registry.ts`**.

I hand out declared surfaces as globs; a glob is a *claim about* a diff, not the diff. Checking the actual file list instead of trusting my fence is the right instinct, and it is now the fourth time this shift that verifying my own words caught something.

Clause ② is **NO and was checked rather than assumed** — `collection.set(storageKey, item)` and `getItem` untouched, precedence pinned in both orders. Refusing the collision was considered and rejected because it would break the sanctioned **ADR-0005** customization path and would be an accept/reject door — a different card, correctly not taken.

### Carried out

**#12431** — the overlay row's own `package_id` is read at hydration but **dropped before `registerItem`** (`mergeArtifactProtection` stamps the artifact's `_packageId`/`_provenance` onto the overlay body first), so the registry **cannot distinguish a deliberate customization from an accidental name collision**. ⭐ That is *why* this card's new message has to state both readings instead of naming the one that happened — a limitation of the fix, traced to its cause and filed rather than hidden. I will triage it.

Flipping to ready and enqueueing once CI converges.
